document.title: feat(bench): Benchmark Mode for the Vita, Vita3K and host
document.summary: Adds Benchmark Mode to the shipping binary: a request file makes the next launch play scripted input against example Deck Apps, time UI frames and the JS loop, write result.json and exit; scripts/bench.sh runs it on the host, in Vita3K or on the Vita and compares against committed baselines. Separately, it deletes the reconciler's always-on method timing.
document.why: Máté wants a performance feedback loop with good metrics and a baseline, mostly for the Vita in the emulator and on the device, with little to no measurement overhead ([request](source:s2)).

sources.label: PR #123
sources.title: feat(bench): Benchmark Mode for the Vita, Vita3K and host
sources.gist: Benchmark Mode, runner, device and Vita3K baselines, and removal of always-on reconciler timing.

sources.label: Claude Code session · Oct 26
sources.gist: Set up a benchmark suite for native and JS performance, mostly Vita via emulator and device, with little to no overhead, to establish metrics and a baseline.

sources.label: perf(runtime): drop the always-on reconciler method timing

lookFor: Perf: [The PR](source:s1) says every hook returns on its first branch when Benchmark Mode is off, but three costs run unconditionally: `event_queue_push` stamps `queued_us`, `process_input_events` reads the clock once per event, and `instance_back_mark_dirty` bumps a counter. Each is one clock read or increment per event or mutation.
`scripts/bench.sh vita` uploads any font or emoji the Vita lacks; on a Vita without them the first run spends most of an hour uploading about 4000 emoji over VitaShell FTP.

parts.name: Benchmark Mode
parts.summary: In-binary scenario runner, timing hooks, runner script, report and baselines.

parts.name: Reconciler timing removal
parts.summary: Deletes the unused ReconcilerMetrics wrapper around every host config method.

groups.title: Benchmark Mode state machine and clocks
groups.why: Measurements have to come from the binary that ships, on a device with no scriptable profiler ([request](source:s2)).
groups.summary: `src/core/bench.c` runs each scenario through boot, setup, warmup, measure and drain using the per-platform `vd_now_us` and `vd_thread_cpu_us` clocks, then writes `result.json`; ADR 0005 records why it lives in the shipping binary.
lookFor: Subtle: on Vita3K `sceKernelGetThreadInfo` reports 0 `runClocks`, so `cpu` is written as null there and the report shows `-`.
Race: the UI and JS threads hand off the window through `g_window` and `g_js_ack` with release/acquire atomics; both flags reset at BOOT to SETUP, after the previous JS thread has been joined.

groups.title: Timing hooks in the UI and JS loops
groups.why: The state machine needs span marks from the render loop and the JS loop, plus commit and input timing from the reconciler.
groups.summary: `main.c`, `render.c`, `js_runtime.c` and `jslib.c` call the `bench_*` marks around existing work, and the reconciler reports commits through `nativeBenchCommit`, while `package_library_set_active_transient` lets a scenario switch Deck App without persisting it.
lookFor: While Benchmark Mode runs, `bench_apply_input` replaces the pad and keyboard polls in `main.c`, so real input is ignored until the run exits.
`main.c` skips `shell_show_home` in Benchmark Mode, so a run never opens on the VitaDeck Shell.

`process_input_events` drains the whole event queue before the loop swaps a snapshot; in `minesweeper-navigate` the backlog never clears, so no swap happens in the window and JS iteration stats are null.

groups.title: Runner, report and docs
groups.why: A feedback loop needs one command per target and a comparison against a baseline ([request](source:s2)).
groups.summary: `scripts/bench.sh` places the request, launches the target and collects `result.json`, and `js/scripts/bench-report.ts` prints it next to the baseline; the skill and AGENTS.md tell agents when to run it.
lookFor: `bench-report.ts` calls a change better or worse only past 10% and past a per-metric absolute noise floor, so small regressions print as a bare percentage.
The Vita path deletes the old `result.json` over FTP and treats only curl exit 78 as a consumed request, so a slow app start does not count as done.

groups.title: Recorded baselines
groups.why: The request asks for a baseline on the emulator and the device ([request](source:s2)).
groups.summary: Generated `result.json` and `meta.json` from one Vita3K run on an i9 MacBook Pro and one device run; skim the meta commit and machine, not the numbers.

groups.title: Drop always-on reconciler timing
groups.why: The wrapper timed every host config call and nothing read the numbers ([commit](source:s3)).
groups.summary: `reconciler-metrics.ts` is deleted, the reconciler passes `hostConfig` straight to `Reconciler`, and `main.tsx` stops logging and exporting the metrics.
lookFor: Breaking: `main.tsx` no longer exports `metrics`, and the reconciler no longer exports `getMetrics` or `resetMetrics`; neither is part of `@vitadeck/sdk`.

commits.subject: perf(runtime): drop the always-on reconciler method timing
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Every host config call went through a wrapper that read getTime() twice and updated a Map, in every run, for a hotspot logger nothing turned on. Benchmark Mode measures commits without it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(bench): Benchmark Mode for the Vita, Vita3K and host
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A request file in the VitaDeck Data Root turns on Benchmark Mode for one launch. It plays scripted pad input against the example Deck Apps, times UI frame spans, JS thread iterations, React commits and input latency in preallocated memory, writes bench/result.json and exits. Off, every hook returns on its first branch.

scripts/bench.sh runs it on the host, in Vita3K or on the Vita over FTP, and prints a report against tests/bench/baselines/<target>.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
